Maya  great detail, thanks for the snapshot. Short answer: continuous batching should help you hit your ~$700 / 1M tokens target in the pilot if we pair the right deployment mode (reserved/dedicated capacity) with conservative latency windows. A few details and a worked example below.

How continuous batching helps (high-level):
- Instead of executing each request independently, the serving runtime holds a brief batching window (milliseconds) to aggregate in-flight work across requests and run them in larger kernels/tiles. That amortizes fixed costs (kernel launch, memory copies) across more tokens and yields much better throughput per GPU.
- For short requests the dominant overhead is per-request setup; batching reduces that overhead and drives down $/1M tokens substantially. For long requests you get fewer opportunities to batch across requests but you still amortize GPU inefficiencies at the sequence level.
- Batching introduces a tradeoff: larger windows increase batching factor (lower cost) but add queuing latency. Our runtime makes this configurable per-route and will automatically route low-latency vs high-throughput traffic to different pools.

Worked example using your numbers (estimates):
- Pilot volume: 200M tokens/month (~6.7M tokens/day). Avg tokens/request = 300 => ~22.2k requests/day => ~0.26 req/sec average.
- Peak bursts: short intervals up to 60 concurrent short requests. During bursts, instantaneous rps can reach several hundred.

Assumptions for two scenarios:
A) Hosted (no reserved capacity), conservative batching factor ~2. Effective $/1M tokens: approx $1,100 (ballpark  depends on model family).
B) Dedicated/reserved capacity with continuous batching and optimized kernels, batching factor ~6 (typical for many short-request workloads at your profile). Estimated effective $/1M tokens: ~$550-750.

What affects batching factor for your workload:
- Concurrency during bursts (the more concurrent short requests, the higher the batching factor).
- Distribution of seq lengths (a heavy tail of long requests reduces batching across short ones unless we route them separately).
- Configured batching window (we typically tune to keep added latency <50-100ms for latency-sensitive routes).

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica will run the pricing model using your attached usage snapshot and the two deployment modes (hosted vs reserved).
2) We can run a short on-prem/remote micro-benchmark that replays your anonymized traffic against a reserved instance to measure real batching factors and latency tail. This takes ~48 hours to schedule and run.
3) If the numbers look good we'll draft a pilot SOW and include a temporary pilot rate that targets your $700 / 1M tokens goal.

I'll attach the populated pricing sheet after Monica runs the sim. Any other constraints (e.g., max allowed queuing latency per route) we should be aware of?
